October 29, 2026 09:00 ET


- Keynote/plenary session and late-breaking poster presentation highlight additional data from Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial of camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) in KRAS-mutated pancreatic cancer
- Additional preclinical poster presentation showcases an expanded application of the AMP-platform in an antigen-agnostic intratumoral treatment approach


BOSTON, Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Elicio Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELTX) (“Elicio” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing next-generation immunotherapies for KRAS-driven cancers, today announced that the Company will conduct a keynote/plenary presentation, as well as two poster presentations showcasing additional results from the randomized Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P study of camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) and an expanded antigen-agnostic intratumoral application of the AMP-adjuvant platform at the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer’s (“SITC”) Annual Meeting. The meeting will take place November 4-8, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona.


**Presentation Details:**


**Keynote/Plenary** **Session**


**Title:** Updates on Clinical Results from the AMPLIFY-7P Study of a Lymph Node-Targeted KRAS Vaccine
**Presenter:** Darrell J. Irvine, PhD, The Scripps Research Institute
**Session Number/Name:** 103: Thomas Waldmann Memorial Plenary Session: Cancer Vaccines, Current and Future
**Presentation Date/Time:** Friday, November 6, 2026, at 10:04 am MT
**Location:** Phoenix Convention Center – North Building – 300 Level – Halls BC


**Late-Breaking Abstract Poster Presentation**


**Title:** Seven valent mKRAS lymph node targeted amphiphile vaccine drives mKRAS-specific T cell responses that correlate with improved clinical outcomes in the AMPLIFY-7P randomized phase 2 trial
**Presenter:** Christopher M. Haqq
**Abstract Number:** 1186
**Session Date/Time:** Saturday, November 7, 2026, 12:30-1:30 pm MT and 6:40-8:10 pm MT
**Location:** Phoenix Convention Center – North Building -Lower Level – Exhibition Halls 4-6


**Poster Presentation**


**Title:** Direct intratumoral delivery of amphiphilic immunomodulators induces durable anti-tumor efficacy
**Presenter:** Martin Steinbuck
**Abstract Number:** 824
**Session Date/Time:** Saturday, November 7, 2026, at 12:30-1:30pm MT and 6:40-8:10pm MT
**Location:** Phoenix Convention Center – North Building – Lower Level – Exhibition Halls 4-6


**About the AMPLIFY-7P Phase 2 Study**


AMPLIFY-7P Phase 2 is a randomized study evaluating camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) versus observation in patients with mutant KRAS-driven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma following completion of standard locoregional therapy. The study enrolled 144 patients across 24 U.S. clinical sites.


**About camupepimut (ELI-002 7P)**


Camupepimut is an investigational, off-the-shelf immunotherapy designed to generate immune responses against seven of the most common KRAS mutations. Camupepimut utilizes Elicio’s proprietary Amphiphile (“AMP”) technology to target mutant KRAS peptide antigens and an immune-stimulatory adjuvant directly to the lymph nodes, where adaptive immune responses are orchestrated.


**About Elicio Therapeutics**


Elicio Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: ELTX) is a clinical-stage biotechnology company advancing next-generation immunotherapies for the treatment of KRAS-driven cancers, including mKRAS-positive pancreatic and colorectal cancers. Elicio intends to build on recent clinical findings in the personalized cancer immunotherapy space to develop effective, off-the-shelf immunotherapies.


Elicio’s AMP technology aims to enhance the education, activation and amplification of cancer-specific T cells relative to conventional immunotherapy strategies, with the goal of promoting durable cancer immunosurveillance in patients. Elicio’s camupepimut lead program is an off-the-shelf immunotherapy candidate targeting the most common KRAS mutations, which drive approximately 25% of all solid tumors.


Off-the-shelf immunotherapy approaches have the potential benefits of low cost, rapid, commercial-scale manufacturing and rapid availability of drug to patients, especially in neoadjuvant settings and for prophylaxis in high-risk patients, contrary to personalized immunotherapy approaches.


Elicio’s pipeline includes additional off-the-shelf therapeutic cancer immunotherapy candidates, including ELI-007 and ELI-008, which target BRAF-driven cancers and p53 hotspot mutations, respectively.
